lessons: Hook with a bold historical or scale anchor (e.g., 'older than the United States') to achieve rewatches near 180%+ at 10%.
Never repeat the video title or hook question right after the start; repeating the premise causes immediate drop-offs of over 30% (e.g., Potato and Pond videos).
Avoid explicit countdowns or 'pause and guess' prompts mid-video, as they consistently trigger viewer drop-off (e.g., Foil and Maple Syrup videos).
Avoid immediate generic filler phrases like 'They are not just there to look cool' or repeated script lines, which lose 28-31% of viewers instantly.
Use high-contrast comparisons between two familiar objects (e.g., Red Tuna vs. White Cod) to sustain high retention into the end (0.86 vs similar).
worst_moment_types: Word-for-word repetition of the main question/hook immediately after the start
Explicit pause prompts and countdowns ('pause and guess... three, two, one')
Low-information filler setup lines ('They are not just there to look cool')
Accidental duplicate narration lines in the script edit
best_hook_types: Historical or extreme scale anchors that reframe common perception ('older than the United States')
Challenging established boundaries or paradigms ('Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge')
Direct visual/sensory contrast setups ('bluefin tuna vs cod meat looking like different animals')
